title: Binary: Computers use 0s and 1s.
body: Binary uses only 0 and 1 to represent values. Computers store many kinds of information as patterns of these two digits.
detail: For example, decimal 2 is binary 10. As a beginner, focus on the idea that computers represent values with patterns of 0 and 1 rather than memorizing conversion formulas first.

title: bit and byte
body: A bit is one 0-or-1 value, and a byte usually groups eight bits. You often see bytes when reading file or memory sizes.
when_to_show: File Size, Memory, and Data Representation Issues
detail: Eight bits usually make one byte. KB, MB, and GB group bytes into larger units, so this idea connects directly to file and memory sizes.

title: Integer: A number without a decimal point
body: An integer (int) is a whole number such as 1, 2, or 100. The text '10' is a string, not the number 10, so the two behave differently.
detail: Python uses int for whole numbers. int('3') converts the string '3' into the number 3. Check quotation marks and int() conversions when a value looks numeric.

title: Integer Overflow
body: An integer overflow is a problem that occurs when a number exceeds the range in which it can be stored. In some languages, the size of integers is fixed, so calculating values that are too large may result in unexpected values or cause errors. While Python’s `int` type handles large numbers relatively flexibly, you must consider range limitations when exchanging data with other languages or systems. When reading code, you must consider the data type of numbers, maximum value limits, and compatibility with external systems. title: Floating-point error
body: Floating-point error is a small discrepancy that occurs because computers cannot accurately represent decimal values. For example, a number like 0.1 may seem simple to humans, but it may not be stored exactly as intended in a computer’s internal binary representation. As a result, the outcome of decimal calculations may differ very slightly from what is expected. In Python, concepts such as `round`, `Decimal`, and tolerance are important when calculating amounts or performing precise comparisons. Be careful when comparing decimals while reading code. This card is not just for memorizing definitions; it serves as a supplementary guide to help you identify how these concepts relate to variables, data types, functions, files, and API flows in actual Python code. When solving problems, first locate the line in the code where this concept appears, and then determine whether that line reads input, modifies a value, evaluates a condition, or stores or outputs a result. Because floating-point numbers store values as approximations, the results of calculations may differ slightly from what a person expects. When reading code, you should verify whether the calculations involve precise monetary values or whether a margin of error is acceptable for comparisons.
when_to_show: float, numerical calculations, data analysis problems
detail: Since `float` stores numbers as approximations, calculations like `0.1 + 0.2` may differ very slightly from what a person would expect. When reading code, be careful when comparing floating-point numbers directly using the `==` operator. For values where accuracy is critical—such as monetary amounts—check whether `Decimal`, rounding, or tolerance criteria are needed.

title: Character Encoding and UTF-8
body: Encoding is the rule used to turn text into stored bytes and back into text. UTF-8 is a common encoding for Korean, English, and many other characters.
when_to_show: open, reading files, Korean character display issues
detail: A file should be read with the same encoding used to save it. When you see open(..., encoding='utf-8') or read_text(encoding='utf-8'), read it as 'interpret the file text as UTF-8.'

title: Stacks and Heaps
body: Stacks and heaps are concepts that come up when explaining how programs use memory. While you don’t need to understand them in great depth at the beginner level, they are helpful for understanding where function calls, local variables, and objects are stored. In Python, you rarely have to manage memory directly, but understanding how objects like lists and dictionaries are associated with variable names makes concepts like shallow copies and mutability easier to grasp. This connects to distinguishing between the values themselves and object references when reading code. title: Compiled Languages and Interpreted Languages
body: Compilation changes code into a form that is easier to execute, while interpretation processes code as it runs. Python implementations can use more than one of these steps.
when_to_show: When reviewing compile, interpreter, python, c
detail: CPython first changes Python source into an intermediate form called bytecode. The Python virtual machine then executes that bytecode. For a beginner, the key idea is simply that Python also has a conversion step before execution.

title: Type System
body: A type tells you what kind of value something is. For example, 3 is an int while '3' is a string, so they can behave differently even if they look similar.
when_to_show: Type, Java Comparison, Python Variable Problem
detail: The same + symbol adds numbers for int values but joins text for str values. When reading code, check quotation marks and conversions such as int(), str(), and type() instead of judging only by how a value looks.

title: Hash Table: Fast Lookup by Key
body: A hash table is a data structure designed to quickly find values using keys. Python dictionaries are also related to the concept of hash tables. While finding a value in a list may require checking from the beginning sequentially, a dictionary is more like a method that uses a key to find a value immediately. For example, you retrieve a value using a key, such as `user['name']`. When reading code, if you encounter a `dict`, you should check which keys exist and how the code handles cases where a key is missing. When solving problems, first locate the line in the code where this concept appears, and then categorize that line: is it a step that reads input, modifies a value, evaluates a condition, or stores or outputs a result? When reading code, it’s helpful to identify which values serve as keys and how the system handles collisions or duplicate keys. It’s a fundamental structure frequently used in searching, caching, counting, and deduplication.

title: Graph: Nodes and Edges
body: A graph is a structure composed of nodes and relationships. A node represents a single entity—such as a concept, person, document, or place—while a relationship shows how those entities are connected.
detail: For example, if “Python,” “list,” and “append” are each a node, “append” can be used to connect them via the relationship that “append adds values to a list.” When reading code, the graph perspective helps you understand the connections between functions and data, files and results, and concepts and examples. title: JSON and JSONL
body: JSON and JSONL are formats frequently used for storing and exchanging data. JSON represents object or list structures as strings, while JSONL places a single JSON object on a single line.
detail: A single JSON file is sufficient for small configuration files, but JSONL can be more convenient for large training datasets or logs. In Python, you can use `json.loads` to convert a string into a dictionary or list, and `json.dumps` to convert it back into a string. When reading code, you must distinguish whether the entire file is a single JSON object or if each line contains a separate JSON object.

title: APIs and REST
body: An API is an interface for exchanging requests and responses. REST is an architectural style that commonly uses HTTP resources, methods, and status codes.
detail: GET often retrieves and POST often submits or creates, but the actual contract defines their meaning; read the endpoint documentation, authentication, input schema, failures, and response format.

title: batch and shard
body: “Batch” and “shard” are terms frequently used when dividing large tasks into smaller parts for processing. A “batch” is a unit consisting of multiple items processed at once, while a “shard” is a large dataset or scope of work divided into multiple pieces. For example, instead of validating 1,000 cards all at once, it is easier to manage them by processing them in batches of 100. When a shard number or batch size appears in the code, you must verify which part of the overall task is being processed and ensure there are no duplicates or omissions. A “batch” is a unit that groups multiple tasks for processing, while a “shard” can be viewed as a fragment of a larger task. When reading the code, you should check the overall scope, the current shard number, completion history, and restart conditions together.

title: mutable / immutable
summary: A mutable value is one whose content can change after it is created, while an immutable value is one whose content does not change after it is created.
examples: When two variables share the same list
body: Lists, dictionaries, and sets are mutable, so a change is visible through every name referencing the same object. Strings, integers, and tuples themselves are immutable, but a tuple can contain a mutable object whose contents still change. Distinguish rebinding a name from mutating an existing object.

title: shallow copy / deep copy
summary: A shallow copy copies only the outer container, while a deep copy copies the inner objects as well.
body: A shallow copy creates a new outer container but shares references to nested objects. copy.deepcopy() recursively copies nested objects, yet custom copy behavior and non-copyable resources mean it is not an unconditional promise that every resource becomes independent. Choose based on the object graph and intended mutations.

title: Matrices and Vectors Code
summary: A matrix is a structure in which numbers are arranged in rows and columns, while a vector is a sequence of numbers arranged in a single direction.
detail: Matrix and vector code is an exercise in understanding how multiple numbers are organized into a specific structure. A vector can be viewed as a single row of values, while a matrix can be viewed as a table with rows and columns. In NumPy, the @ operator is used for matrix multiplication and frequently appears in code involving coordinate transformations, embeddings, and Kalman filters. Start by confirming the dimensions and the meanings of rows and columns.
body: Matrices and vectors are basic structures for organizing and working with multiple numbers. You can think of a vector as a line of numbers, and a matrix as a table where numbers are arranged in rows and columns. A list of a single student’s scores can be viewed as a vector, while a score sheet for multiple students can be viewed as a matrix.
